title: ESO’s Very Large Telescope peers into a distant nebula
caption: The Omega Nebula, Messier 17, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: M 17, Messier 17, Omega Nebula · constellation Sagittarius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Vast clouds of gas and dust, lit by the intense radiation of young stars, give this view of Messier 17 the look of a painting. The nebula, also called the Omega or Swan Nebula, lies in Sagittarius, the Archer, about 6000 light-years from Earth. This picture shows a central region about 15 light-years across, while the whole nebula spans about 40 light-years.

At the centre is a cluster of massive young stars whose radiation makes the surrounding hydrogen glow. To its lower right lies a huge cloud of molecular gas. In visible light its dust blocks the view, but in infrared the hydrogen glow behind it shines faintly through.

Hidden in that dark reddish region, astronomers found the silhouette of an opaque disc of gas and dust. It looks small here but is about 20 000 AU across, dwarfing our Solar System. The disc is thought to be rotating and feeding material onto a protostar, a star in the making.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.13 x 6.20 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 9.8 × 9.9 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image was made with the ISAAC instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope. The J filter (1.25 microns) is shown in blue, H (1.6 microns) in green and K (2.2 microns) in red.
filters: 1.25 μm · Infrared J (Very Large Telescope ISAAC)
1.6 μm · Infrared H (Very Large Telescope ISAAC)
2.2 μm · Infrared K (Very Large Telescope ISAAC)
understand.eye: All three bands are infrared, invisible to the eye, and infrared light passes through dust that blocks visible light, revealing glowing gas hidden from ordinary view.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: One AU equals the average Earth-Sun distance. Messier 17 is also a popular target for amateur astronomers, who can capture good images of it with small telescopes.
alt: Clouds of gas and dust around a central cluster of bright young stars, with a dark reddish cloud to the lower right.
